subject: ss-rheumatology-immunology
title: Pregnancy and reproductive health in rheumatic disease

steps.tx: Preconception counseling in systemic lupus erythematosus mandates maintaining quiescent disease or low disease activity for at least **6 months** prior to conception. Planning pregnancy during stable remission significantly minimizes maternal lupus flares, renal relapses, preeclampsia, fetal growth restriction, and preterm birth.
steps.say: Preconception counseling requires stable disease remission for at least 6 months before conception. This significantly reduces maternal flares, preeclampsia, and preterm delivery.

vis.alt: Maternal systemic lupus erythematosus counseling and pregnancy timing
vis.caption: Maintaining stable disease remission for 6 months prior to pregnancy optimizes maternal-fetal outcomes. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: **Hydroxychloroquine** is safe and strongly recommended throughout pregnancy and lactation in all women with SLE. Continuation of hydroxychloroquine lowers maternal flare rates, reduces preeclampsia risk, and **halves the recurrence risk of congenital heart block** in mothers carrying anti-Ro/SSA antibodies.
steps.say: Hydroxychloroquine is safe and continued throughout pregnancy and breastfeeding. It prevents disease flares, lowers preeclampsia risk, and halves congenital heart block recurrence.

rows: Reduces risk of gestational lupus flares by >50%
Improves endothelial function and trophoblast invasion
Halves congenital heart block recurrence in anti-Ro+ mothers

steps.tx: Transplacental crossing of maternal **anti-Ro/SSA** and **anti-La/SSB** antibodies causes neonatal lupus erythematosus. The most severe permanent complication is **congenital complete third-degree heart block**, which develops irreversibly between **16 and 26 weeks of gestation** due to antibody-mediated autoimmune myocarditis and atrioventricular nodal fibrosis.
steps.say: Transplacental maternal anti-Ro antibodies cause neonatal lupus. The most severe complication is congenital complete heart block, which develops between 16 and 26 weeks of gestation.

nodes.label: Maternal anti-Ro/SSA antibodies cross placenta at 16 weeks gestation
Autoantibody binding to fetal cardiomyocytes and calcium channels
Irreversible AV nodal calcification and complete congenital heart block

steps.tx: Serial fetal echocardiography is recommended **every 1 to 2 weeks from 16 to 26 weeks gestation** in anti-Ro/SSA-positive pregnancies to detect emerging PR interval prolongation. Emerging first- or second-degree heart block warrants immediate maternal treatment with fluorinated oral **dexamethasone at 4 mg daily**, which crosses the placenta unmetabolized to arrest inflammatory nodal injury.
steps.say: Serial fetal echocardiography every 1 to 2 weeks from 16 to 26 weeks detects early AV block. Incomplete heart block is treated with transplacental dexamethasone 4 mg daily.

left.title: Fluorinated steroids (Dexamethasone)
points: Dose 4 mg daily for emerging heart block
Inhibits active fetal carditis and second-degree block

right.title: Non-fluorinated steroids (Prednisolone)
points: Minimal fetal exposure; ideal for maternal flares
Ineffective for treating fetal cardiac nodal inflammation

steps.tx: In obstetric antiphospholipid syndrome, pregnancy with recurrent early miscarriages is treated with **low-dose aspirin combined with prophylactic low-molecular-weight heparin**. In women with a history of thrombotic APS, **therapeutic doses of low-molecular-weight heparin** are mandatory throughout pregnancy, converting back to warfarin postpartum.
steps.say: Obstetric antiphospholipid syndrome requires low-dose aspirin and prophylactic low-molecular-weight heparin. Women with prior thrombosis mandate therapeutic-dose heparin.

rows: Resume long-term oral anticoagulation with warfarin

steps.tx: Immunosuppressive medications safe throughout pregnancy comprise **hydroxychloroquine, azathioprine at 2 mg/kg/day or less, sulfasalazine, cyclosporine, and tacrolimus**. Non-fluorinated glucocorticoids like **prednisone** are largely degraded by placental 11-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2, treating maternal flares with minimal fetal exposure.
steps.say: Pregnancy-compatible immunosuppressants include hydroxychloroquine, azathioprine, sulfasalazine, and calcineurin inhibitors. Prednisone is largely degraded by placental enzymes.

rows: Safe for acute maternal inflammatory flares
Must be discontinued prior to planned conception

steps.tx: Teratogenic antirheumatic medications must be discontinued well prior to conception. **Methotrexate** must be stopped at least **1 to 3 months** prior to conception. **Mycophenolate mofetil** must be stopped at least **6 weeks** prior, while **leflunomide** mandates an accelerated **cholestyramine washout of 8 g three times daily for 11 days**.
steps.say: Teratogenic drugs must be stopped prior to conception: methotrexate 1 to 3 months before, mycophenolate 6 weeks before, and leflunomide requires cholestyramine washout.

nodes.label: Methotrexate stopped 1 to 3 months preconception with high-dose folate
Mycophenolate mofetil stopped at least 6 weeks before conception
Leflunomide cholestyramine washout: 8 g TID for 11 days until drug level <0.02 mg/L

steps.tx: **Certolizumab pegol** is a PEGylated Fab fragment of an anti-TNF antibody lacking an Fc portion. Because placental transfer requires Fc receptor binding, certolizumab exhibits **minimal to absent transplacental transfer** throughout all trimesters, making it the preferred anti-TNF biologic for women desiring pregnancy or breastfeeding.
steps.say: Certolizumab pegol lacks an Fc region and shows zero to minimal placental transfer. It is the preferred anti-TNF biologic throughout pregnancy and lactation.

left.title: Certolizumab pegol
points: PEGylated Fab fragment without Fc portion
Zero active transport across placental FcRn
Safe to continue through all three trimesters

right.title: Full-length IgG1 biologics (Infliximab/Adalimumab)
points: Active transplacental FcRn transport after week 20
High fetal serum levels if given in late pregnancy
Discontinued at week 20-30 to avoid infant immunosuppression
